name: Facet
text: Make the timeline strip a horizontal bar at the top, fixed height, always visible. It shows the entire project duration in one glance, letting users see where they are and what’s coming next without scrolling or hunting. The trade-off is less vertical space for other panels, but the clarity and speed of orientation outweigh that loss.

name: Pane
text: Fixed-height strips bury critical detail when users zoom into dense data—users lose context fast. A collapsible, resizable strip with a "focus mode" toggle keeps visibility without locking away depth; test it with real users scrolling through Manus’s dark-themed graphs to see if clarity or speed breaks.

name: Facet
text:
We should use a collapsible, resizable timeline strip with a "focus mode" toggle, as this allows users to balance context and detail according to their needs. This approach is better than a fixed-height strip because it preserves vertical space for other panels when users need to zoom into dense data. The trade-off is added complexity in the interface, which we're accepting in order to prevent users from losing context when dealing with detailed information. By testing this design with real users interacting with Manus's dark-themed graphs, we can validate that clarity and speed are maintained.

name: Pane
text: A collapsible, resizable strip with a "focus mode" toggle may introduce complexity, overwhelming users with too many options and modes to manage. The real risk is that users may struggle to find the right balance between context and detail, leading to frustration and decreased productivity. Testing this approach with real users and comparing it to a simple, adaptive strip that automatically adjusts its size based on the user's zoom level could settle the argument and reveal the most effective solution.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Fixed-height timeline strip at the top of EXCAVA, always visible, with a single "Focus Mode" toggle to collapse it when users need vertical space for dense data.

The result must deliver a clear, unmissable project overview at all times, with one click to reclaim screen real estate for deep dives. Own it: Facet (visualization-w1).
